To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the NNLO soft function for the production of a boson with large transverse momenta in hadronic collisions can be written as a sum of two functions, one of them is the soft function of the boson production at threshold and the other one is the soft function for the boson plus one parton production at threshold, and the NNLO soft functions are expressed in terms of the NNLO soft anomalous dimensions and the NLO soft anomalous dimension.

we have calculated the soft function at NNLO for electroweaks bosons at a hadron collidor, and we have performed the first NNLO calculation of a soft function that describes emissions in three different directions, and we have computed this soft function for the first time at NNLO.
we have calculated the NNLO soft function describing the production of electroweak (γ, W,Z or H) bosons with large transverse momenta at a hadron-hadron collider.

the development of the theory of quantum chromodynamics (QCD), a theory that describes the interaction between the strong force and the elementary particles that carry it, quarks and gluons.

the present paper provides a new result for the soft function of the production of a massive vector boson at a hadron-hadron collider.

the soft function is given by a double integral over the phase space of two massless final state partons.

we have completed the computation of all the three building blocks (hard, jet, and soft functions) needed for the resummation of electroweak processes with a large transverse momentum of the final-state boson.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the soft function can be factorized into a universal part and an event-specific part.
the soft function is dominated by a single soft gluon with transverse momentum p T ∼ m W, where m W is the electroweak scale.
